AUTHOR: Bilodeau, SM; Schwartz, AWH; Xu, BF; Pauca, VP; Silman, MR
TITLE: A low-cost, long-term underwater camera trap network coupled with deep residual learning image analysis
DATA: Own DEAC time-lapse camera-trap images (130,621 collected; 88,899 usable; 10,727 train + 2,702 validation hand-sorted)
V_EV: Results: 'camera function was also limited by reduced visibility at certain sites, which varied based on local turbidity and light availability, and by depth.'
D_EV: Methods: 'Our model was trained on a sample of 10,727 images sorted by our team ... validated ... 2,702 images hand-sorted by trained volunteers.'
R_EV: Methods: training and validation images both drawn from the same DEAC deployments at Lighthouse Reef; no external dataset evaluated
C_EV: Methods: 'validated by comparing the categories produced by sorting above and below 0.5 probability with the actual "Fish" and "NoFish" designations'
E_EV: Image analysis: 'Images with a "Fish" probability of 0.5 or above were used to determine the relative presence of fishes at camera sites inside and outside of the ... MPA'
ARCH: ResNet-50 binary classifier with focal loss
NOTE: Split only given as image counts from time-lapse series; unit not stated -> coded image-level (per rule for image counts without grouping); verify. ~32% of images excluded as unusable (biofouling) by visual examination; treated as fouling, not water-visibility exclusion (P1 not applied) - verifier may consider V_ALL=N. Diver surveys (independent UVC) were compared to human-identified images, NOT to AI output, so E5=없음. AI-derived ecological outputs: proportion of fish images by habitat/MPA (occupancy-like) and seasonal time series (Fig 7) -> E1=복수. FNR derivable from Table 1 (Fish class 72.9% accuracy).
